candidate_goals.name: Mouse-Directed Movement and Cursor Targeting
candidate_goals.description: Replace the WASD-only CharacterController movement in PlayerMovement.cs with mouse-directed click/hold movement projected onto the gameplay plane, and expose a reusable cursor-world-target reference for future spell aiming/targeting, per the GDD's 'Move and Aim' requirement.
candidate_goals.implementation_scope: Rewrite PlayerMovement.cs input handling to read mouse position instead of WASD keys, raycast/project the cursor onto the gameplay plane, and move the CharacterController toward that point on click or hold. Expose the resolved cursor-world-point publicly so future spell-aiming code can read it. Single behavior: click/hold-to-move plus cursor-target exposure; no spell logic included.

dependencies.reasoning: The CharacterController substrate is unaffected by the input scheme change; it remains a valid movement executor for a mouse-directed destination-follow approach.

dependencies.evidence: DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.BuildCamera() creates a default perspective camera at (0,8,-8) rotated (45,0,0), not the GDD's required fixed orthographic isometric projection.
dependencies.reasoning: A cursor-to-plane raycast works under any camera type, so the wrong-paradigm camera can serve as a disposable stand-in for testing click/hold-to-move; it is not a hard blocker, but the projection math will likely need retuning once the real isometric camera exists.

current_state.implemented_summary: Only Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/ contains real gameplay code, implementing a single-room sealed-door interaction prototype: PlayerMovement.cs drives a CharacterController with WASD-only keyboard input (no mouse-directed click/hold movement and no cursor-world targeting anywhere in the project), a foundational mismatch against the GDD's required 'Move and Aim' mouse-directed control scheme. PlayerHealth.cs implements a working CurrentHealth/TakeDamage/Damaged pattern but has no death/restart hook and there is no mana system anywhere. DoorInteractable.cs implements a complete, tested 5-second hold-to-open state machine (progress tracking, cancel on movement/damage) but has no closing, locking, durability, or breaking logic -- only opening exists. PlayerInteractionController.cs wires E-key hold-to-interact to the door with range detection. DoorInteractionUI.cs shows a prompt and progress bar. DebugDamageControl.cs is an explicit debug/test-only damage trigger, not a combat system. DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs (an Editor script) procedurally builds the entire scene -- a perspective Main Camera at (0,8,-8) rotated (45,0,0) that is NOT configured as the GDD's required fixed orthographic isometric projection, a primitive Unity Plane 'Floor' and two primitive Cube 'Walls' that are a disposable test room rather than the required Isometric Tilemap-based world representation, a Capsule-visual Player, a Cube door visual, and a Canvas UI. This builder has actually been run: Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity was inspected directly and contains serialized GameObjects named Walls, DoorRoot, Player, Main Camera, EventSystem, Canvas, and Floor, confirming this is real current scene state, not just builder capability. No Tilemap/Grid/Tile assets, no NavMesh bake or NavMeshAgent/NavMeshSurface component, no sprite/character art, no PixelLab-generated assets, no spells (Fireball/Frost Field/Force Wave), no mana system, no enemies (Melee or Ranged), no multi-room floor, and no death/restart logic exist anywhere under Assets/ -- confirmed via a full Assets/**/* glob and targeted greps. Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity (Directional Light + Camera only) and Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity (Unity's default template) are unrelated, unused leftover scenes.

selected_goal.name: Mana Resource System (Pool, Spend, Post-Cast Regen)
selected_goal.description: Implement a reusable Mana component (max/current mana, Spend(amount), regeneration that resumes after a fixed post-cast delay), mirroring the existing PlayerHealth pattern, ready for the three required spells (Charged Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) to consume.

selection_reason: Among the seven candidates, only Mana, Fixed Isometric Camera, and Door Close-Lock-Break are simultaneously prerequisites_ready=true, resource_acquisition_readiness=high, foundation_compatibility=compatible, expected_rework_risk=low, and implementation_risk=low. Mouse-Directed Movement matches on readiness but has foundation_compatibility=mixed and expected_rework_risk=medium because it rests on the current perspective test camera as a disposable stand-in. Isometric Tilemap World Foundation and Melee Enemy are both required and high-unlock, but Tilemap carries medium implementation_risk/expected_rework_risk and low integration_readiness as the project's first Tilemap authoring attempt, and Melee Enemy is blocked outright (prerequisites_ready=false) by a missing walkable-world hard prerequisite, which is why that prerequisite is promoted into its own candidate (Isometric Tilemap World Foundation) rather than absorbed. Between the three top-tier, equally low-risk candidates, Mana was selected over Door Close-Lock-Break because Door's unlock_value is medium (a leaf feature nothing else depends on), while Mana's unlock_value is high. Mana was selected over Fixed Isometric Camera because, although both share identical prerequisites_ready/resource_acquisition_readiness/prototype_readiness/integration_readiness/foundation_compatibility/expected_rework_risk/implementation_risk values, Camera's downstream unlock is concentrated in the visual/art-authoring layer (Tilemap alignment, sprite sorting) that the GDD explicitly decouples from gameplay/simulation logic, whereas Mana is a genuine shared prerequisite for three entirely missing required gameplay-code features (Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) -- the actual core combat/resource-management loop the GDD's design pillars center on ('wait for mana to regenerate,' 'decide when to fight, flee, or risk opening the next sealed door'). This is a close, honestly-tied call on structured readiness; it is decided by which system's unlock is more mechanically central to required gameplay code, not by any weakness in Camera.

advantages.reasoning: Mana unlocks three required gameplay-code spell systems directly; camera correctness primarily unlocks visual/art-authoring validation (Tilemap alignment, sprite sorting) that the GDD explicitly decouples from gameplay/simulation logic, so no required gameplay-code feature is mechanically blocked by an imperfect camera today.

Mana's pool/spend/regen behavior integrates and can be meaningfully tested today; the Tilemap foundation's real validation (sprite sorting, camera alignment, room integration) remains largely unproven as the project's first Tilemap authoring attempt.
Mana mirrors the already-proven PlayerHealth pattern with low rework risk, while the Tilemap foundation is a first attempt at a new authoring workflow likely to need tuning as camera and art evolve.

Mana is a small self-contained component; the Tilemap foundation bundles Grid/Tilemap setup, placeholder art acquisition and import, and a decoupled walkability layer, a larger scope with more surface area for issues.
Mana has no unmet hard prerequisite; Melee Enemy's hard prerequisite (a walkable navigable world) is missing_prerequisite.
Mana can be meaningfully tested today with a debug trigger; Melee Enemy cannot be meaningfully tested without a navigable surface consistent with the required architecture.
Mana extends the existing compatible PlayerHealth pattern; Melee Enemy's core dependency (world navigation) is either absent or a known-disposable placeholder.
Mana has low rework risk; any navigation baked for Melee Enemy over the temporary primitive test room would very likely need to be redone once the real Tilemap/navigation foundation exists.
Mana integrates today at medium readiness; Melee Enemy's integration readiness is low, even further from real encounter-space validation such as Bone Archive lane widths or Chapel of Ash occlusion.

winner_tradeoffs.summary: Mana was not chosen because rival candidates were structurally weaker across the board -- against Fixed Isometric Camera it is an honest tie on every readiness/risk dimension, decided only by which unlock is more central to required gameplay code. Against Isometric Tilemap World Foundation and Melee Enemy, Mana has genuinely better readiness and risk profiles, while those two candidates carry real, disclosed weaknesses (higher risk/rework for Tilemap; an outright missing hard prerequisite for Melee Enemy, whose foundation is promoted into its own candidate rather than silently absorbed).

evidence: PlayerHealth.cs (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/PlayerHealth.cs) implements CurrentHealth/TakeDamage/Damaged with no analogous mana pool anywhere in the project.

A full Assets/**/* glob combined with grep for 'Mana', 'Fireball', 'Frost', 'Force', and 'Enemy' across Assets/NoSafeCircle found zero real matches (the only 'Mana' hit was a false-positive substring inside 'SceneManagement').

DebugDamageControl.cs (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/DebugDamageControl.cs) demonstrates the project's existing pattern for a small debug-trigger component (K key -> TakeDamage), directly reusable as the pattern for a debug mana-spend trigger to test the new Mana component standalone.

GDD Section 2 ('Resources, Feedback, and Failure') states 'Mana regenerates slowly after a brief post-cast delay,' Section 3 lists 'mana regeneration' as required scope, and Section 5 ('Runtime Implementation') states 'Mana will regenerate through a local gameplay system after the defined post-cast delay.'

GDD Section 2's 'Spell and Enemy Interactions' table describes all three required spells (Charged Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) as costing/consuming mana, making a shared Mana pool a genuine shared prerequisite for all three, none of which currently exist in Assets/.

Unlike Mouse-Directed Movement (rests on the incompatible perspective test camera) or Melee Enemy (blocked by a missing navigable world), this candidate depends on no camera, Tilemap, NavMesh, or enemy-related asset that is currently missing or incompatible.

rejected_high_priority_alternatives.name: Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup
rejected_high_priority_alternatives.reason_rejected: Matches Mana on every readiness and risk dimension (prerequisites_ready=true, resource_acquisition_readiness=high, prototype_readiness=high, integration_readiness=medium, foundation_compatibility=compatible, expected_rework_risk=low, implementation_risk=low), but its unlock_value is medium rather than high: correcting the camera primarily unlocks visual/art-authoring validation (Tilemap alignment, sprite sorting), which the GDD explicitly decouples from gameplay/simulation logic, so no required gameplay-code feature is mechanically blocked by it today.

rejected_high_priority_alternatives.name: Isometric Tilemap World Foundation (First Room)
rejected_high_priority_alternatives.reason_rejected: Shares Mana's high unlock_value and true prerequisites_ready, but has lower integration_readiness (low vs. medium) and higher expected_rework_risk and implementation_risk (medium vs. low) as the project's first attempt at Tilemap authoring, Grid/collision decoupling, and placeholder art import in one bounded slice.

rejected_high_priority_alternatives.name: Melee Enemy Chase-and-Attack Prototype
rejected_high_priority_alternatives.reason_rejected: Rejected because prerequisites_ready=false: its hard prerequisite, a walkable navigable world, is missing_prerequisite (no NavMesh bake, NavMeshAgent, or NavMeshSurface exists anywhere, and the only floor is a disposable primitive test room). Building that walkable world is itself the substantial, independently testable Isometric Tilemap World Foundation candidate, not local plumbing for this enemy, so the prerequisite was promoted rather than absorbed.
